correctness.rationale: Shen–Wang Proposition 2.2 was confirmed for both words: marginal membership is gp_{λi}∈Z(G). Multiplying two such elements gives the stated quotient rectangle, with exactly z² ordered pairs above each failing ordered row/column quadruple. Row ratios u_{λi}u_{μi}^{−1} are constant exactly for pairs of left-equivalent rows; transitivity follows by multiplying the constant left factors in order. For a partition of d into at least two positive sizes, the cross-class ordered-pair count is at least 2(d−1), with equality only for sizes 1,d−1, by maximizing the sum of squares. Applying this first to the rows and then to column-ratio batches gives the product bound and forces one exceptional row and one exceptional column. More explicitly, first divide each column on the right by its entry in a reference ordinary row; ordinary rows now have constant entries, and the exceptional row's entries are constant except at one column. Scaling each row on the left makes all these constants 1. Under any left-row/right-column gauge change the normalized quotient matrix changes only by a uniform conjugation (by the multiplier at column 1). Normalizing the one-cell perturbation produces either its interior row/column or the entire respective interior when it is on a distinguished axis; the four cases yield a common value t or t⁻¹ on the product support. Conversely all listed products arise this way. The only duplicated support choice is at size 2. An arbitrary quotient matrix is determined by its normalization and r+c−1 boundary entries, and each free G-coordinate has z lifts. Division by (zq)^(rc) verifies the probabilities. If Q is trivial or either matrix dimension equals one there is no failing rectangle.
residual_risks: The counts concern ordered product pairs and labeled matrices over a finite group, not isomorphism classes or sandwich matrices with zeros.

value.rationale: This quantitatively separates the first possible nonclosure from exact closure in a setting where the qualitative criterion was known. A sharp uniform gap alone gives an obstruction; classifying all cases and counting them also determines the precise low-defect probabilities for random labeled matrices. The dimensions, central lift and noncommutative gauge invariance are intrinsic to the problem rather than arbitrary enumeration choices.
residual_risks: No downstream classification of the full defect spectrum or of semigroup isomorphism types is established.
